$comment: Every Pulumi stack that exists in a branchLeft state backend, with the
secrets provider and state backend each one uses today.
This file is the enumeration the migration off GCP KMS depends on. It is
checked in because the alternative — discovering the set from a `pulumi
stack ls` at execution time — only lists the stacks in whichever backend
the workstation was last logged into, and there is more than one backend.
A stack absent from this file is a stack nobody re-wraps, and after the
KMS key is destroyed its committed ciphertext is undecryptable forever.
`config_path` is repo-relative and may be null: some stacks generate their
`Pulumi.<stack>.yaml` on a CI runner and never commit it, and PUL-12 means
even a fully migrated passphrase stack's committed file carries no
`encryptionsalt` — salt-injected-at-deploy is the mandated end state, not
a gap. Either way nothing in the committed tree can prove the provider for
that stack, so its `terminal_state` can only be satisfied by an
`attestation`: an operator statement recorded here under review in git,
not something read out of a file.

stacks.note: Salt-injected-at-deploy: CI appends the passphrase salt from a repository secret immediately before the first `pulumi` command and never commits it, so the committed file reads `absent` by design.

attestation.evidence: secrets_providers read directly from the gs://branchleft-pulumi-state checkpoint: passphrase, 32 resources.

stacks.note: The only stack that outlives the GCP estate. State moved off gs://branchleft-pulumi-state to the Hetzner backend per RUNBOOK-existing-stack-migration.md Part B, and the backend is now pinned in mail/Pulumi.yaml. CI applies on merge (mail-plan/mail-apply in ci.yml) and appends the passphrase salt from the PULUMI_SALT_MAIL repository secret; hand-gated stack operations append it from the operator's own copy.

attestation.evidence: secrets_providers read directly from the gs://branchleft-pulumi-state checkpoint: passphrase, 4 resources.

stacks.note: Salt-injected-at-deploy, same pattern as branchleft-shared-infra. Two `secure:` ciphertexts (SMTP submission credential) stay committed -- PUL-12 permits that; nothing in the file lets an attacker derive the key without the salt beside it.

attestation.evidence: secrets_providers read directly from the gs://branchleft-pulumi-state checkpoint: passphrase, 45 resources.
secrets_providers read directly from the gs://branchleft-pulumi-state checkpoint: passphrase, 27 resources.

stacks.note: Config is reconstructed on each CI run from the exported deployment and never committed. Re-wrapped onto the passphrase provider; branchLeft/workspace#128 tracked the work that got the reconstruction script to accept a passphrase-managed stack. config_path stays null, so unlike every other attested entry here this one has no file for the attestation to ever disagree with -- a rollback to gcpkms would not turn this finding red on its own; re-verify by hand before relying on it.

attestation.evidence: pulumi stack change-secrets-provider passphrase completed ("Migrating old configuration and state to new secrets provider") and pulumi stack export --show-secrets succeeded afterwards; secrets_providers read back from the gs://branchleft-pulumi-state checkpoint: passphrase, salt prefix v1:v6UAjuKhH, 12 resources. Wrapped by ghost-platform's existing repo-level passphrase; the stored copy was independently re-typed from the password manager and verified against the live checkpoint.

stacks.note: Densest secrets of the set: two secret config values and roughly 33 encrypted values in state. Lives in its own bucket, so a sweep driven by one `pulumi stack ls` misses it entirely. Re-wrapped onto the passphrase provider; branchLeft/workspace#128 tracked the work. Superseded by a successor stack later in the programme, so its terminal state accepts either a re-wrap or a destroy-and-archive.

attestation.evidence: Re-wrapped the same way as branchleft-ghost-provisioning/blog; pulumi stack export --show-secrets succeeded afterwards. secrets_providers read back from the gs://branchleft-blog-pulumi-state checkpoint: passphrase, salt prefix v1:rLDLxMTFD, matching the value placed in the PULUMI_SALT_BLOG repository secret, 33 resources. Wrapped by a newly minted 32-character passphrase, escrowed in the platform owner's password manager and set as PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE on branchLeft/ghost-tenant-blog before the re-wrap; the stored copy was independently re-typed and verified. Post-merge deploy green: "Restore the stack's encryption salt" and the delete-guard both passed, and Apply reported 31 unchanged with no creates, updates, deletes or replaces.

stacks.note: Born on the passphrase provider and never wrapped by the KMS key -- terminal_state never-kms, satisfied without an attestation, because demanding one from a stack with no KMS dependency to migrate away from is exactly the 'gate red in its own success state' failure the rest of this script exists to avoid. hetzner/Pulumi.production.yaml is committed (landed via branchLeft/shared-infra#4) and holds non-secret configuration only -- no `encryptionsalt`, so the file reads `absent`, which reports `needs-attestation` -- not drift -- and never-kms accepts that on its own, same as the estate entry below.

Born on the passphrase provider, same as the network stack -- never-kms, satisfied without an attestation. Unlike the network stack, hetzner/estate/Pulumi.production.yaml IS already committed on main today: it holds non-secret configuration reviewed ahead of the stack existing, with no `encryptionsalt` because the stack has not been created. `config_path` points at it: the file reads `absent` (no secretsprovider, encryptedkey or encryptionsalt), which reports `needs-attestation` -- not drift -- and never-kms accepts that on its own.

backend_reference_sites.note: `pulumi login gs://branchleft-pulumi-state` in the edge stack's deploy-plan and deploy-apply jobs. The mail jobs never log in: their backend is pinned in mail/Pulumi.yaml.
Pins its own backend rather than relying on the ambient login; mail/Pulumi.yaml and hetzner/estate/Pulumi.yaml do the same.

Pinned when the stack's state moved off gs:// (RUNBOOK-existing-stack-migration.md Part B) and its CI apply path landed — the pin is what the mail-plan/mail-apply jobs rely on instead of a `pulumi login` step.
The estate's own project. Pins the same backend as hetzner/Pulumi.yaml deliberately: it resolves a stack reference to the network stack, and a stack reference resolves inside one backend only.
The scanner names the backends it matches on. Enumerated rather than exempted: an exemption would also hide a real login step added to it later.

external_backend_reference_sites.note: Two separate `pulumi login` steps — preview job and deploy job. Both must change if the shared bucket is ever retired.
Logs in twice: the shared bucket for the provisioning stack, then the tenant's own bucket templated from a repository variable.

`pulumi login gs://$PULUMI_STATE_BUCKET`, from a repository variable set per tenant at provisioning time. Generated into every tenant repo, so changing it here does not change any repo already generated.
The generated copy of the template workflow. Already diverged from the template by generation, so it is its own site.
Comment documents the PULUMI_STATE_BUCKET contract; generated into every tenant repo.

provider_selection_sites.note: Was `pulumi stack select "$TENANT" --create`, selecting the shared KMS key via its --secrets-provider flag, for the provisioning stack. Retired by branchLeft/ghost-platform#81 to select the passphrase provider instead, reading ghost-platform's own repo-level PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE.

Was `pulumi stack init "$TENANT"`, selecting the shared KMS key via its --secrets-provider flag, for the tenant's own stack. Retired by branchLeft/ghost-platform#81 to select the passphrase provider instead, minted fresh per tenant and written to that tenant repo's own PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE secret.
